questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was curious to learn a language similar to danish, to have the opportunity to work in Norway in the future. And I really love the Norwegian nature and the aspect that Norway and Denmark are quite similar regarding culture and it was not that far away from home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All in all it was a great experience! And I wouldn't be without it, but it was also a bit lonely and hard at times to make new friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - and you could just email UiO if you had any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a buddy week and a buddy group, so you had a group of 10-15 people you knew and could sightsee in Oslo with in the first couple of weeks, so that was really nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Because of the covid situation we had no big gathering or anything at the campus, so I haven't been at campus a lot.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy - through SiO (Student in Oslo)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was not a long way with a bicycle or with the T-bane (metro) maybe around 9 min. I lived in Kringsjå student housing, so I was very nice, close to Sognsvann (a very nice lake) and a lot of hikes near by. I really enjoyed a lot of time there, but it is a bit more away from the city center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was cheap, but I had hoped it was a bit more social. I lived in a dorm, where we shared the kitchen, but we had no dinners together or nothing social - so that was a shame! The people I lived with was nice, but everybody lived their own lives.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was not that easy, because I did not get the courses I really wanted, so it is a good idea to have a plan B.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing at first, but if you keep in touch with someone from UiO, then they will help you or register you.  At first I found some interesting courses I really wanted before applying, but then it turned out they were shut down and not available at UiO anymore. Not so good communication about that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Phone and email correspondence from UiO.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got two courses I wanted, but then I wanted to chance in the beginning and it was not possible.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a plan B for the courses, you can never be really sure what you get.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses were not really relevant for my studies, but it was okay. I attended a master class for 20 ECTS points and I think the academic level was a bit too low for me and my studies.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Somehow or a bit lower compared to the level in UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar, seminars, lectures and group work

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SNE3200 Education for learners with special needs
PSY2500 Kommunikasjon, språk og samfunn

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the PSY2500 course (language psychology) - very nice lectures and professors and it was very interesting and the exam was a written home paper, where you could choose the exact topic you found most interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything - everything is just so much more expensive. Of course I knew that - especially beers and alcohol, but just everyday shopping and living in Norway are way more expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The gym membership was quite cheap and there is also a swimming pool and a lot of teams to join! Around 150 DKK per month.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The gym was nice and cheap and there is a lot of different sports you can encounter if you want.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the gym or a sport team - I wanted to join volleyball, but I never did. I think it would be easier to make new friends - other exchange students and Norwegians too.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just all the nature around Oslo is amazing. In winter you can ski everywhere and in the summer you can hike everywhere. Vettakollen is a nice viewing point close to Kringsjå and Sognsvann and all the islands in the Oslo fjord are nice and cozy in the summer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - it is very similar to danish culture and the language is almost the same :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really because I did not do it so much, maybe join a sports team is my best advice. The Norwegians can be a bit shy and closed.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A nice and slow living, enjoying the nature on Sundays and Oslo is a nice, small city with a lot of beautiful nature around.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open, enjoy and do not study so much, that you don't have time to enjoy your life in a new and different city!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the cold and dark winter times in january!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Enjoying the nature, living a slow life and not had to work beside my studies.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my family and friends back home - and having zoom lectures in the beginning of the semester was terrible, when you are alone in your little room in some dorm.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do it

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
